title: Care Management Tier Placement and Re-stratification Policy
content:
**Care Management program policy.** A member referred to Care Management is placed in one tier, and may later be re-stratified to another, under the following clauses. The figures each clause reads — risk score bands, chronic condition minimums, placement precedence numbers, the emergency visit and admission triggers and the graduation months — are the figures set for each Care Management tier.

## 1. Placement

1.1 A member is placed in the tier with the lowest placement precedence number whose conditions the member meets.

1.2 The conditions are, in this order: nursing facility level of care, a Health Home qualifying condition, pregnancy or the postpartum year, then the risk score band together with the chronic condition minimum.

1.3 A risk-banded tier is met only when the member's predictive risk score lies within the tier's band and the member also has at least the tier's minimum number of chronic conditions; the two parts are read together.

## 2. Re-stratification

2.1 A member who reaches the tier's emergency department visit trigger within 6 months, or the tier's inpatient admission trigger within 12 months, is re-stratified to the next higher risk tier. Either trigger on its own is enough.

2.2 A member who meets the tier's graduation stable months steps down one tier.

## 3. What a re-stratification keeps

3.1 A re-stratification keeps the episode, its care plan and its contact history. It records the member's new tier and the risk score at the time of the re-stratification on the same episode; it does not open a new episode.

## Illustrations (hypothetical members)

| Member's circumstances | Tier the placement clause selects |
|---|---|
| Nursing facility level-of-care determination, and pregnant | LTSS Service Coordination — nursing facility level of care comes first |
| Pregnant, with a predictive risk score in the Complex Case Management band and enough chronic conditions for it | Maternal Care Management — pregnancy or the postpartum year comes before the risk score band |
| No nursing facility level of care, no Health Home qualifying condition, not pregnant or postpartum; score and chronic condition count both within Care Coordination Level 2's figures | Care Coordination Level 2 |

**Trigger truth table** (for a tier whose triggers apply):

| Emergency visit trigger reached within 6 months | Admission trigger reached within 12 months | Re-stratified to the next higher risk tier |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | No | Yes |
| No | Yes | Yes |
| Yes | Yes | Yes |

A hypothetical member re-stratified in March from one tier to the next keeps the episode opened at referral, the care plan signed earlier and every contact already recorded; the record changes the tier and the risk score only.
